quests.sentence: By the time I arrived, the meeting had already started.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had started is the past perfect form, showing the meeting began before I arrived, an earlier point in the past.
quests.nativeTip: One event finished before another past event took place — which one came first?
quests.example: By the time I arrived, the meeting had already started.

quests.sentence: When she opened the fridge, she realized she had forgotten to buy milk.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had forgotten is the past perfect form, describing an earlier past action that explains a later past realization.
quests.nativeTip: The forgetting happened earlier than the moment she opened the fridge.
quests.example: When she opened the fridge, she realized she had forgotten to buy milk.

quests.sentence: She went to the store right after realizing this.
quests.ruleExplanation: Went is the simple past form, describing the next event in a sequence that's already clear from the word 'after'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Right after' already makes the order clear, so no earlier-past form is needed here.
quests.example: She went to the store right after realizing this.

quests.sentence: He had already left the building before the fire alarm went off.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had left is the past perfect form, stressing that the action was fully finished before the other past event.
quests.nativeTip: This emphasizes that leaving was complete before the alarm, an even earlier point.
quests.example: He had already left the building before the fire alarm went off.

quests.sentence: He left the building before the fire alarm went off.
quests.ruleExplanation: Left is the simple past form; since 'before' makes the sequence clear, the past perfect isn't required.
quests.nativeTip: 'Before' already tells us the order, so ask whether an earlier-past marker is really necessary here.
quests.example: He left the building before the fire alarm went off.

quests.sentence: After the alarm went off, everyone evacuated within minutes.
quests.ruleExplanation: Evacuated is the simple past form, describing an action that followed another in a clearly ordered sequence.
quests.nativeTip: 'After' already clarifies the order between these two actions.
quests.example: After the alarm went off, everyone evacuated within minutes.

quests.sentence: When I got to the station, the train had already left.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had left is the past perfect form, showing the train's departure happened before I arrived at the station.
quests.nativeTip: Think carefully about which event happened first — did the train leave before or after arrival?
quests.example: When I got to the station, the train had already left.

quests.sentence: When I got to the station, the train left.
quests.ruleExplanation: Left is the simple past form here, suggesting the departure happened at or right after the moment of arrival.
quests.nativeTip: Without 'had', this suggests the train left right around the time of arrival, not earlier.
quests.example: When I got to the station, the train left.

quests.sentence: The train had left five minutes earlier, so I had to wait for the next one.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had left is the past perfect form, marking an action completed before the later past consequence.
quests.nativeTip: One event is clearly placed before the other past situation it caused.
quests.example: The train had left five minutes earlier, so I had to wait for the next one.

quests.sentence: Maria couldn't find her keys because she had left them at work.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had left is the past perfect form, explaining an earlier cause behind a later past situation.
quests.nativeTip: The reason for her problem happened at an earlier point in the past.
quests.example: Maria couldn't find her keys because she had left them at work.

quests.sentence: Maria called her office and asked a coworker to check her desk.
quests.ruleExplanation: Called is the simple past form, describing the next step in a straightforward sequence of events.
quests.nativeTip: These actions happened in the order they're told, without needing an earlier reference point.
quests.example: Maria called her office and asked a coworker to check her desk.

quests.sentence: By the time the coworker checked, someone had already picked up the keys and handed them to security.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had picked up is the past perfect form, showing this happened before the coworker checked the desk.
quests.nativeTip: One action was already complete before the coworker's action took place.
quests.example: By the time the coworker checked, someone had already picked up the keys and handed them to security.

quests.sentence: By the time the ambulance arrived, a bystander had already started CPR.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had started is the past perfect form, showing the CPR began before the ambulance's arrival.
quests.nativeTip: One action was already underway and complete before the ambulance showed up.
quests.example: By the time the ambulance arrived, a bystander had already started CPR.

quests.sentence: By the time the fire department arrived, the flames had spread to the second floor.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had spread is the past perfect form, marking an earlier development that occurred before another past event.
quests.nativeTip: The spreading happened before the firefighters got there.
quests.example: By the time the fire department arrived, the flames had spread to the second floor.

quests.sentence: The flames spread quickly once they reached the wooden staircase.
quests.ruleExplanation: Spread is the simple past form, describing a single past event told in its natural order.
quests.nativeTip: This describes one continuous sequence without needing an earlier reference point.
quests.example: The flames spread quickly once they reached the wooden staircase.

quests.sentence: I had never seen snow before I moved to Vermont.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had never seen is the past perfect form, describing a lack of experience up until an earlier past event.
quests.nativeTip: This experience — or lack of one — is measured up to an earlier point in the past.
quests.example: I had never seen snow before I moved to Vermont.

quests.sentence: I moved to Vermont for a new job two years ago.
quests.ruleExplanation: Moved is the simple past form, describing one finished action at a stated past time.
quests.nativeTip: This states a single completed event with a specific past time.
quests.example: I moved to Vermont for a new job two years ago.

quests.sentence: Within a month, I had already learned to drive in the snow.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had learned is the past perfect form, showing the skill was gained before a later reference point.
quests.nativeTip: This achievement was complete by a certain earlier point in the past.
quests.example: Within a month, I had already learned to drive in the snow.

quests.sentence: I woke up, brushed my teeth, and made coffee, all before 7 a.m.
quests.ruleExplanation: Woke, brushed, and made are simple past forms, describing a sequence in the order it occurred.
quests.nativeTip: These events are told in the order they happened, so no earlier-past form is needed.
quests.example: I woke up, brushed my teeth, and made coffee, all before 7 a.m.

quests.sentence: I had already made coffee by the time my alarm even went off, because I couldn't sleep.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had made is the past perfect form, stressing that the coffee was ready before the alarm even sounded.
quests.nativeTip: This action was finished before another past event, which is worth emphasizing since it's unusual.
quests.example: I had already made coffee by the time my alarm even went off, because I couldn't sleep.

quests.sentence: She ate breakfast after she showered.
quests.ruleExplanation: Ate is the simple past form; the word 'after' removes any need for the past perfect here.
quests.nativeTip: 'After' already makes the order between these two actions obvious.
quests.example: She ate breakfast after she showered.

quests.sentence: The engine stalled because the mechanic hadn't replaced the worn belt.
quests.ruleExplanation: Hadn't replaced is the negative past perfect form, explaining an earlier omission that caused a later problem.
quests.nativeTip: The missing repair happened, or rather didn't happen, before the stalling.
quests.example: The engine stalled because the mechanic hadn't replaced the worn belt.

quests.sentence: The mechanic promised to replace it the following week.
quests.ruleExplanation: Promised is the simple past form, describing one completed past statement.
quests.nativeTip: This is a single reported statement placed in its own point in the past.
quests.example: The mechanic promised to replace it the following week.

quests.sentence: By the time the warranty expired, the company had fixed the same issue three times.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had fixed is the past perfect form, describing repeated actions completed before a later past point.
quests.nativeTip: These repeated repairs all happened before the warranty's expiration.
quests.example: By the time the warranty expired, the company had fixed the same issue three times.

quests.sentence: The lights were already off when we got home; someone had turned them off earlier.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had turned off is the past perfect form, explaining an earlier cause behind the situation we found.
quests.nativeTip: The explanation refers to an action that happened even before we arrived.
quests.example: The lights were already off when we got home; someone had turned them off earlier.

quests.sentence: We got home around midnight after the concert ended.
quests.ruleExplanation: Got is the simple past form, describing an event in a sequence whose order is already clear.
quests.nativeTip: 'After' makes the order between these events clear on its own.
quests.example: We got home around midnight after the concert ended.

quests.sentence: I recognized her immediately because we had met once, years earlier, at a conference.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had met is the past perfect form, describing a much earlier past experience that explains a later past event.
quests.nativeTip: The earlier meeting happened well before the moment of recognition.
quests.example: I recognized her immediately because we had met once, years earlier, at a conference.

quests.sentence: The manuscript looked untouched, but an editor had actually reviewed every page overnight.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had reviewed is the past perfect form, showing the review was already complete before the manuscript was seen.
quests.nativeTip: Appearances can be misleading — something happened earlier than it seems.
quests.example: The manuscript looked untouched, but an editor had actually reviewed every page overnight.

quests.sentence: The editor left a few notes in the margins before returning it.
quests.ruleExplanation: Left is the simple past form, describing an action told in the natural order of the story.
quests.nativeTip: This continues the story in a straightforward order without needing an earlier reference point.
quests.example: The editor left a few notes in the margins before returning it.

quests.sentence: None of us realized how much work had gone into it until we read the notes.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had gone is the past perfect form, describing effort completed before it was later discovered.
quests.nativeTip: The effort happened before anyone found out about it.
quests.example: None of us realized how much work had gone into it until we read the notes.
